summary: The S. 689 bill, known as the Tule River Tribe Reserved Water Rights Settlement Act of 2025, recognizes and settles the water rights of the Tule River Indian Tribe in California by approving a 2007 water rights settlement agreement between the tribe, the South Tule Independent Ditch Company, and the Tule River Association. The legislation outlines a specific tribal water right to divert and use up to 5,828 acre-feet of water per year from the South Fork Tule River, establishes a federally funded trust fund for water development projects and operation and maintenance, transfers specific federal and tribally owned lands into trust for the benefit of the tribe, and requires waivers and releases of certain legal claims.

affected_groups.effect: Receives recognized and quantified water rights, substantial funding for water development and maintenance, land transferred into trust, and specific legal waivers in exchange for settling water claims.
Participate in the water rights settlement agreement, coordinate on operation rules, and accommodate senior water rights as specified in the agreement and court decrees.
affected_groups.group: Downstream Water Users (including Tule River Association and South Tule Independent Ditch Company)

affected_groups.effect: Tasked with executing the settlement agreement, managing the trust fund, transferring specified federal lands into trust, and issuing trust deeds.
affected_groups.group: Federal Agencies (Secretary of the Interior and Secretary of Agriculture)

key_provisions: Ratifies and confirms the 2007 water rights settlement agreement involving the Tule River Tribe, the South Tule Independent Ditch Company, and the Tule River Association.
Establishes a tribal water right allowing the diversion and use of up to 5,828 acre-feet of surface water per year from the South Fork Tule River.
Establishes the Tule River Indian Tribe Settlement Trust Fund with separate accounts for water development projects and operation, maintenance, and replacement (OM&R).
Appropriates and transfers $518,000,000 for water development projects and $50,000,000 for OM&R, subject to cost indexing adjustments.
Transfers specified Bureau of Land Management lands, Forest Service lands in the Sequoia National Forest, and tribally owned fee lands into trust for the benefit of the tribe.

Requires the Tule River Tribe and the United States as trustee to execute waivers and releases of specified water rights claims and damages claims against the United States, the state, and other entities.

Grants the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of California exclusive jurisdiction to review and approve the agreement, resolve disputes, and select operation rules if parties reach an impasse.
missing_information: Exact timelines for when appropriations will be requested or disbursed beyond the general terms of the bill are not specified.
Specific local economic or environmental impacts on non-participating regional water users outside of the defined downstream parties are not detailed.
